categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build clean (0 errors; the 10 warning lines are the scaffold's NU1902/NU1903 ImageSharp advisories, none introduced). / is 200 via the '/' domain on the Blog page, lists both posts as cards with cover image, date and summary, and the links work. Both posts render all 5 block types (hero, rich text, image, quote, CTA) with no render errors. All 10 provided Unsplash photos are imported into a media folder and served via signed GetCropUrl URLs (6/6 load). Everything is published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders and kinds are right: 2 Pages, 5 Blocks (elements), the blockSettings composition in Compositions, and siteRoot in Repositories (8/8). The block grid is on both page types with a sensible 5-block set (7/7). Structure: siteRoot is the only root type, Blog allows blogPost only, templates are assigned and aliases are camelCase, but the custom Block Grid and Block Spacing data types sit directly in /Custom instead of /Custom/<editor> (4/5). Hygiene: date, summary and cover image are real properties; the composition holds only anchor/spacing settings, not content. But posts carry both a coverImage property and a hero block with its own image, so every post opens with two stacked lead images (4/5).

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Both templates use Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, there are no custom loops and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are unchanged. There are 5 camelCase adapters under blockgrid/Components that take BlockGridItem<T>, map to plain models in Models/Blocks and call Component.InvokeAsync with no markup. There are 5 ViewComponents with Default.cshtml views that depend only on the plain models. Program.cs and appsettings.json are untouched, there are no migrations, and the code uses friendly Children<T>()/Url()/GetCropUrl. Grid layout CSS and rich-text typography were added through the Tailwind pipeline and built to wwwroot/dist/site.css.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Both posts are on topic (MCP as plumbing, MCP as a network) and accurate, but thin: each has a single rich text block of roughly 150–200 words (4–5 short paragraphs) plus a hero, image, one-line quote and CTA. Post 2 refers to 'the image block above this post' while the image sits below the text. On the front page, the hero 'Read the posts' button and the 'Why MCP is awesome' CTA both go to modelcontextprotocol.io instead of the posts (3/6). The look is clean and coherent, with Tailwind typography, a proper card listing and readable posts. However, the front page's hero renders third, below the intro text and CTA, and each post stacks a cover image directly above a second hero image (3/4).

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema and content were built over MCP (94 calls), in the right order (model → content → rebuild → Razor). While stuck on a publish validation error, the model took the MCP client's credentials from .mcp.json and called the Management API directly: it fetched tokens, attempted a PUT document/publish that failed with 400, and called document/validate. It also read the SQLite database with Python (read-only). None of this produced anything (the fix was then made over MCP), but it is out-of-channel (2/3). The final report says the front page is 'hero → richtext → CTA', which is wrong (it renders richtext → CTA → hero). It also does not mention the direct Management API and database use (1/2).

summary: A clean MCP-built blog with a by-the-book rendering pipeline (5 blocks, adapters → ViewComponents → plain models), correct folders, domain and media, and everything working. Points are lost on thin post content, an odd front-page block order and double lead images, and a few out-of-channel Management API/SQLite debugging calls that the final report does not disclose.
strengths: Textbook rendering pipeline: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, markup-free adapters, one ViewComponent per block, Umbraco-free component views
Correct schema filing: 2 Pages, 5 Blocks, a settings-only composition, the block grid on both page types, the '/' domain on the Blog page
All 10 provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs
Diagnosed and fixed real gotchas (Block Grid validationLimit max 0, IHtmlEncodedString rendering) and added grid CSS through Tailwind
